required_concepts.definition: The CyberAlchemy Orchestrator is a general agent-orchestration product that lets a participant author, review, admit, execute, observe, recover, and reuse bounded multi-agent and tool strategies through one control plane while preserving the distinct owners of meaning, effects, evidence, acceptance, and promotion.
required_concepts.formal: Orchestrator = authoring + admission + durable_execution + observation + recovery; authority_effect(Orchestrator) = none by identity
required_concepts.plain_language: The product turns a reviewed strategy into a visible, recoverable run.
required_concepts.domain_context: A user may create a two-lane dialectic, research swarm, software workflow, or other bounded strategy through the same contracts.
required_concepts.boundary: The Orchestrator does not decide domain truth, grant effect authority, or make every worker result accepted.

required_concepts.definition: The Local Orchestrator Edition is the first supported deployment envelope: one trusted host, one logical accepted-history writer per run stream, file-backed durable records, and explicitly configured local or Gateway-backed adapters.
required_concepts.plain_language: The first edition runs within one controlled host boundary.
required_concepts.domain_context: A local operator can run and recover strategies while using optional remote model execution through an explicit Gateway adapter.
required_concepts.boundary: Local does not imply production readiness, remote authentication, distributed consensus, or exactly-once external effects.

required_concepts.definition: A Run Bundle is an immutable content-addressed envelope binding one admitted strategy instance, compiled Work Graph, semantic work identity, run identity, limits, adapter requirements, inputs, authority references, engine version, and source digests.
required_concepts.formal: RunBundle = hash(strategy_instance, graph, work_identity, run_id, limits, adapters, inputs, authority_refs, engine_version, sources)
required_concepts.plain_language: It freezes everything required to know what was admitted for one run.
required_concepts.domain_context: The controller registers a run from the exact bytes of one bundle.
required_concepts.boundary: A Run Bundle is not mutable runtime state, an attempt, a receipt, or evidence that execution occurred.

required_concepts.definition: Semantic Work Identity is the stable identity of one immutable Work meaning and version, independent of its runs and attempts.
required_concepts.plain_language: It names the job as meant, regardless of how many times it runs.
required_concepts.domain_context: A saved research strategy retains one meaning identity across distinct runs until meaning-changing bytes change.
required_concepts.boundary: A retry does not create a new Semantic Work Identity; changed meaning does.

required_concepts.definition: An Orchestrator Run is one registered lifecycle of one exact Run Bundle under one stable run identity and admission reference.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is one managed journey of an admitted bundle.
required_concepts.domain_context: The Control Center follows one run from admission through structural completion and lifecycle closeout.
required_concepts.boundary: A run inherits neither acceptance nor external-effect authority from another run.

required_concepts.definition: An Execution Attempt is one separately identified try to execute or reconcile one addressed Command Intent within a run.
required_concepts.formal: Attempt = (attempt_id, run_id, command_id, lease, fence, outcome?)
required_concepts.plain_language: Every retry gets its own truthful identity and history.
required_concepts.domain_context: A failed agent turn may lead to a new attempt with a new lease and fence.
required_concepts.boundary: Retry, rerun, replay, resume, and reconciliation are distinct operations.

required_concepts.definition: Accepted Structural History is the ordered append-only sequence of accepted structural events and their atomically bound cursors and complete command batches for one run stream.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the sole durable input from which structural progress is replayed.
required_concepts.domain_context: The controller commits an accepted agent event and every resulting command together.
required_concepts.boundary: It is not automatically domain truth, effect success, product acceptance, or a second lifecycle ledger.

required_concepts.definition: A Command Receipt is an immutable typed report binding the exact run, attempt, command, worker fence, executor, authority reference, inputs, outputs, proposed events, effect disposition, and observation times.
required_concepts.formal: Receipt = hash(run, attempt, command, fence, executor, inputs, outputs, proposed_events, effect, times)
required_concepts.plain_language: It records exactly what a worker reports about one command attempt.
required_concepts.domain_context: An agent adapter returns a receipt that the controller can validate before accepting any event.
required_concepts.boundary: A valid receipt does not accept its event, judge its meaning, approve its result, or prove an external effect beyond its evidence.

required_concepts.definition: A Reconciliation Decision is an owner-issued digest-bound resolution of an interrupted attempt or unknown effect that states the known effect disposition and whether a distinct next attempt may proceed.
required_concepts.plain_language: An owner resolves uncertainty the runtime cannot safely guess about.
required_concepts.domain_context: After a worker disconnects during an external action, the effect owner decides whether a retry is safe.
required_concepts.boundary: Lease expiry, timeout, scheduler preference, or process exit cannot create this decision.

required_concepts.definition: A Lifecycle Ledger records execution, structural closeout, result acceptance, promotion, release, and deployment as separate ordered facts with independent prerequisites and owners.
required_concepts.formal: LifecycleLedger = ordered_facts(execution, closeout, acceptance, promotion, release, deployment)
required_concepts.plain_language: It prevents one successful stage from pretending later decisions happened.
required_concepts.domain_context: A completed research run can remain unaccepted and undeployed.
required_concepts.boundary: A generic PASS value cannot represent every lifecycle stage.

required_concepts.definition: A Current-State Projection is a rebuildable non-authoritative read model combining run identity, structural state, pending commands, attempts, leases, receipts, blockers, costs, and lifecycle facts with provenance.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the operator view reconstructed from preserved records.
required_concepts.domain_context: The run page shows current progress and links every statement to its source record.
required_concepts.boundary: The projection cannot schedule, accept history, repair state, grant authority, or rewrite its sources.

required_concepts.definition: The Orchestration Lab is the explicitly non-operational area containing examples, research strategies, fixtures, witness results, and diagnostic visualizations used to learn about Orchestrator behavior.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the workshop for trying and explaining strategies.
required_concepts.domain_context: Robot Talks and Robot World fixtures can demonstrate generic contracts without becoming product modes.
required_concepts.boundary: A Lab PASS is not product acceptance, release, deployment, provider quality, or production readiness.

required_concepts.definition: Effect Disposition is an evidence-supported statement that an addressed command’s external effect is not_applied, applied, or unknown.
required_concepts.formal: EffectDisposition in {not_applied, applied, unknown}; unknown => retry_blocked
required_concepts.plain_language: It says what is actually known about a consequence outside the Orchestrator.
required_concepts.domain_context: Recovery keeps a command blocked while its external write remains unknown.
required_concepts.boundary: Effect disposition is not inferred solely from exit status, timeout, missing receipt, or cancellation request.

required_concepts.definition: A Strategy is a declarative, versioned coordination design that specifies an intended outcome, lanes, Work composition, policies, limits, evidence expectations, and result reduction without admitting or executing a run.
required_concepts.formal: Strategy = (outcome, lanes, work, policies, limits, evidence, reduction)
required_concepts.plain_language: It describes how participants should work together for a class of problems.
required_concepts.domain_context: A dialectic strategy defines two opposing lanes and a synthesis step.
required_concepts.boundary: A Strategy is not a running DAG, worker assignment, authority grant, or accepted conclusion.

required_concepts.definition: A Strategy Template is a reusable parameterized Strategy definition with declared input fields, defaults, constraints, compatibility requirements, and version identity.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is a reusable recipe for creating a concrete strategy.
required_concepts.domain_context: The user saves a two-lane dialectic template and later supplies a new question.
required_concepts.boundary: A template is not a concrete dispatch, run, mutable form state, or proof that the strategy is effective.

required_concepts.definition: A Template Version is the immutable identity and compatibility contract of one exact Strategy Template state.
required_concepts.plain_language: It pins the exact reusable recipe used to create a proposal.
required_concepts.domain_context: Existing runs continue to name version 1 after version 2 changes its lanes.
required_concepts.boundary: A display-name edit may be metadata; a meaning-changing edit requires a new version.

required_concepts.definition: Template Instantiation is the deterministic binding of validated parameter values and selected compatible adapters to one Template Version, producing a Strategy instance or validation failure.
required_concepts.plain_language: It fills a reusable recipe with concrete values before review.
required_concepts.domain_context: A user supplies the idea, budget, and agent profiles for a dialectic template.
required_concepts.boundary: Instantiation does not admit, dispatch, execute, or grant authority.

required_concepts.definition: A Dispatch Proposal is a reviewable concrete orchestration proposal that binds a Strategy instance, compiled preview, lane and agent requirements, limits, adapters, inputs, evidence expectations, and requested authority references.
required_concepts.formal: DispatchProposal = review(strategy_instance, graph_preview, requirements, limits, adapters, inputs, authority_refs)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the exact plan shown before a run is admitted.
required_concepts.domain_context: Control Center shows the two lanes, four agents, synthesis step, budget, and boundaries for approval.
required_concepts.boundary: A proposal is not admission, execution, an effect authorization, or a worker command.

required_concepts.definition: Run Admission is the owner-controlled decision that one exact Dispatch Proposal may be materialized as a Run Bundle and registered as an Orchestrator Run within stated limits.
required_concepts.plain_language: It turns a reviewed proposal into a registered run contract.
required_concepts.domain_context: The operator admits the exact strategy bytes and budget shown in Control Center.
required_concepts.boundary: Admission does not authorize undeclared external effects, accept future results, or promote artifacts.

required_concepts.definition: A Lane is a named logical coordination channel within a Strategy that groups Work by role, concern, stance, ordering, or reduction relationship.
required_concepts.plain_language: It explains why a group of tasks exists and how it relates to other groups.
required_concepts.domain_context: Constructive and adversarial agents occupy separate tension lanes before synthesis.
required_concepts.boundary: A Lane is not a worker process, queue partition, permission boundary, or physical location.

required_concepts.definition: An Agent Assignment is the versioned binding of one agent identity and declared capabilities to one addressed Command Intent, lane, and Execution Attempt.
required_concepts.plain_language: It says which agent is asked to do which exact work this time.
required_concepts.domain_context: A research agent is assigned to the constructive lane for attempt 2.
required_concepts.boundary: Assignment does not prove capability quality, transfer domain authority, or authorize effects beyond the command envelope.

required_concepts.definition: A Work Definition is an immutable versioned description of one typed unit of Work, its input and output contracts, body, limits, authority requirements, and completion events.
required_concepts.formal: WorkDefinition = (identity, input, output, body, limits, authority_requirements, completion_events)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the stable structural meaning of one task or composite.
required_concepts.domain_context: The same synthesis Work Definition can appear in many Strategy instances.
required_concepts.boundary: It is not a mutable run, attempt, permission grant, worker, or implementation process.

required_concepts.definition: Composite Work is a Work Definition whose body contains a bounded composition of other Work Definitions while preserving the same external input, output, event, and identity contract as leaf Work.
required_concepts.formal: CompositeWork is WorkDefinition where body = bounded_composition(WorkDefinition*)
required_concepts.plain_language: A workflow can be reused wherever a single task can be used.
required_concepts.domain_context: A research lane can contain search, critique, and report Work yet expose one result contract.
required_concepts.boundary: Composite Work does not create unbounded recursion, child authority, or a second root history owner.

required_concepts.definition: A Work Graph is a validated versioned structural composition of Work Nodes and Work Connections with explicit mappings, release policies, roots, terminals, and bounds.
required_concepts.formal: WorkGraph = DAG(nodes, connections, mappings, release_policies, roots, terminals, bounds)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the executable structural form compiled from a Strategy and Work definitions.
required_concepts.domain_context: The graph fans four agents out, joins their reports, then releases synthesis.
required_concepts.boundary: It is not runtime state, domain truth, communication permission, or an independently authored replacement for its source.

required_concepts.definition: A Work Node is one addressed occurrence of a Work Definition within a Work Graph with graph-local identity, bindings, dependencies, and release configuration.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is one placement of reusable Work inside a graph.
required_concepts.domain_context: Two lanes may use the same analyst Work Definition through distinct nodes.
required_concepts.boundary: A node is not the reusable Work Definition, worker, attempt, or result.

required_concepts.definition: A Work Connection is a typed directed relation that maps one declared Structural Event or output reference from a source node to a target node input or release condition.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the labeled wire that carries structural progress between nodes.
required_concepts.domain_context: A completed critique event contributes one input to a quorum synthesis join.
required_concepts.boundary: A connection does not transfer domain authority, prove payload truth, or execute the target.

required_concepts.definition: A Release Policy is the declared deterministic rule—such as all, any, or quorum—that decides when a Work Node becomes structurally eligible from accepted predecessor outcomes.
required_concepts.formal: eligible(node) = policy(accepted_predecessor_outcomes); policy in {all, any, quorum(k), explicit_gate}
required_concepts.plain_language: It states how much accepted predecessor progress is enough to release a node.
required_concepts.domain_context: Synthesis requires all four lane reports, while a fallback may accept any successful provider.
required_concepts.boundary: Release eligibility is not scheduling priority, domain approval, result acceptance, or effect authority.

required_concepts.definition: An Event Proposal is a worker-reported typed candidate fact linked to one command, attempt, fence, outputs, and evidence for validation by the Orchestrator Runtime.
required_concepts.formal: EventProposal = (event_type, payload_ref, command_id, attempt_id, fence, evidence_refs)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is what a worker asks the controller to consider as having happened.
required_concepts.domain_context: An agent receipt proposes ReportProduced with the report digest.
required_concepts.boundary: A proposed event has not entered Accepted Structural History and cannot advance RWO.

required_concepts.definition: An Accepted Structural Event is an Event Proposal that passed the runtime’s identity, schema, attempt, fence, authority-reference, and duplicate/conflict checks and was atomically appended with its Structural Transition.
required_concepts.formal: AcceptedEvent = validate(EventProposal, run, attempt, fence, schema, authority_refs)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the structural fact RWO is allowed to use.
required_concepts.domain_context: The controller accepts ReportProduced and commits the resulting cursor and synthesis command.
required_concepts.boundary: Acceptance for structural routing is not domain truth, result approval, or proof of an external effect.

required_concepts.definition: A Structural Transition is the pure deterministic result of applying one Accepted Structural Event to one Work Graph and Orchestration Cursor, yielding the next cursor and complete zero-or-more Command Intent batch.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is RWO’s answer to “what becomes structurally ready next?”
required_concepts.domain_context: The fourth accepted lane report closes a quorum and releases one synthesis command.
required_concepts.boundary: A transition does not persist itself, execute commands, judge outputs, or grant authority.

required_concepts.definition: An Orchestration Cursor is the rebuildable versioned structural projection of satisfied connections, node outcomes, released nodes, issued command identities, and terminal state for one run.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the compact structural position that replay can reconstruct.
required_concepts.domain_context: Recovery rebuilds the cursor from accepted history and compares it with stored state.
required_concepts.boundary: The cursor is not authoritative domain state, a scheduler queue, approval, or lifecycle acceptance.

required_concepts.definition: A Command Intent is an immutable addressed request produced by a Structural Transition that names the Work Node, inputs, limits, required capabilities, authority references, and expected receipt/event contract.
required_concepts.formal: CommandIntent = (command_id, node_id, input_refs, limits, capability_requirements, authority_refs, receipt_contract)
required_concepts.plain_language: It describes an action the runtime may schedule.
required_concepts.domain_context: RWO emits one command asking a compatible agent to synthesize four reports.
required_concepts.boundary: A Command Intent is not execution, assignment, a lease, a successful effect, or permission beyond its referenced envelope.

required_concepts.definition: RWO Core is the internal independently tested package that owns Work composition, graph validation, Structural Event reduction, cursor semantics, release policies, command generation, and engine-version replay compatibility.
required_concepts.formal: RWOCore = compile(WorkDefinition*, Strategy) + transition(WorkGraph, Cursor, AcceptedEvent)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the pure structural kernel reused by the Orchestrator Runtime.
required_concepts.domain_context: The runtime calls RWO Core after validating an event and before atomically storing the transition.
required_concepts.boundary: RWO Core does not own storage, scheduling, workers, providers, frontend, ARE, domain meaning, lifecycle acceptance, or external effects.

required_concepts.definition: The Orchestrator Runtime is the durable control-plane implementation that owns run registration, accepted-history transactions, attempts, leases, scheduling, receipts, recovery, lifecycle records, APIs, and adapter coordination while calling RWO Core for structural decisions.
required_concepts.formal: Runtime = controller + history_port + scheduler + coordination + recovery + lifecycle + API + adapters
required_concepts.plain_language: It makes admitted strategies run durably and visibly.
required_concepts.domain_context: The runtime validates an agent receipt, asks RWO Core for the transition, stores it, and schedules resulting commands.
required_concepts.boundary: The runtime does not redefine RWO semantics, domain truth, product definitions, or owner authority.

required_concepts.definition: The Accepted-History Port is the sole runtime interface authorized to atomically accept an expected cursor, one Accepted Structural Event, the next cursor, and the complete Command Intent batch for one stream.
required_concepts.formal: accept(expected_cursor, event, next_cursor, commands) -> Accepted | Duplicate | Conflict
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the one door through which structural history advances.
required_concepts.domain_context: The file-backed implementation rejects a stale cursor instead of splitting event and command state.
required_concepts.boundary: An implementation of the port is not a second reducer, domain ledger, or lifecycle decision store.

required_concepts.definition: A Worker is an addressed runtime participant that accepts a Command Intent through a declared adapter and returns a typed Command Receipt.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is anything the scheduler can ask to perform one bounded command.
required_concepts.domain_context: A local process, tool adapter, model-backed agent, or human-task adapter may act as a Worker.
required_concepts.boundary: Worker identity does not imply intelligence, authority, capability quality, or successful execution.

required_concepts.definition: An Agent is a Worker whose command execution includes a bounded reasoning or policy process over supplied context and declared capabilities.
required_concepts.formal: Agent subset Worker; execute = reason_or_apply_policy(context, command, limits)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is a reasoning-capable worker operating inside the same checked boundary as other workers.
required_concepts.domain_context: An ARE Gateway-backed agent produces a structured report and proposed event for one command.
required_concepts.boundary: An Agent cannot mutate the DAG, accept its own event, grant authority, or declare its result true by producing it.

required_concepts.definition: An Agent Capability is a versioned declaration of an operation an Agent can attempt, together with input, output, limit, evidence, and compatibility contracts.
required_concepts.formal: AgentCapability = (capability_id, version, input_contract, output_contract, limits, evidence_contract, compatibility)
required_concepts.plain_language: It tells the scheduler what kind of work an agent claims it can receive.
required_concepts.domain_context: A research capability declares web-retrieval outputs and budget obligations.
required_concepts.boundary: A capability declaration is not permission, availability, quality evidence, assignment, or authority.

required_concepts.definition: An Agent Turn is one bounded request-response interaction with an Agent within one Execution Attempt, carrying exact command, context, tool, budget, and result references.
required_concepts.formal: AgentTurn = (turn_id, attempt_id, request_digest, context_refs, tool_policy, budget, response_digest)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is one traceable reasoning interaction inside an attempt.
required_concepts.domain_context: The Gateway receives a prompt and returns one structured report for the assigned lane.
required_concepts.boundary: A turn is not the entire attempt, agent identity, accepted event, conversation authority, or persistent memory by default.

required_concepts.definition: A Capability Adapter is a versioned boundary that translates one Command Intent into a selected worker or provider protocol and translates its output into a Command Receipt without changing structural meaning.
required_concepts.plain_language: It connects the runtime to a concrete executor while preserving contracts.
required_concepts.domain_context: A Gateway adapter maps an agent command to the remote API and returns a typed receipt.
required_concepts.boundary: An adapter does not select domain meaning, broaden authority, manufacture evidence, or alter the Work Graph.

required_concepts.definition: A Worker Lease is a time-bounded exclusive claim that allows one Worker to perform one Execution Attempt for an addressed Command Intent.
required_concepts.plain_language: It prevents multiple workers from treating the same command as their active attempt.
required_concepts.domain_context: The scheduler leases a synthesis command to one agent until its deadline.
required_concepts.boundary: A lease is not external-effect authority, proof of liveness, result acceptance, or permission after expiry.

required_concepts.definition: A Worker Fence is a monotonic attempt token bound to a Worker Lease that lets the runtime reject stale or superseded receipts.
required_concepts.plain_language: It makes an old worker unable to finish a newer attempt accidentally.
required_concepts.domain_context: A late receipt from attempt 1 is rejected after attempt 2 receives a higher fence.
required_concepts.boundary: A fence does not cancel an external effect already applied or prove what happened outside the runtime.

required_concepts.definition: A Recovery Assessment is the deterministic classification of persisted run, history, transaction, lease, receipt, and effect evidence after interruption into resumable, completed, conflicted, or owner-reconciliation-required state.
required_concepts.plain_language: It determines what the runtime can safely know after restart.
required_concepts.domain_context: Startup replay finds an issued command with unknown effect and blocks it for owner resolution.
required_concepts.boundary: An assessment does not repair state, choose an owner decision, or infer unknown external effects.

required_concepts.definition: A Recovery Action is an explicit digest-bound next operation selected from a Recovery Assessment, such as resume scheduling, accept a recorded event, quarantine a result, or request reconciliation.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the reviewable next step after recovery analysis.
required_concepts.domain_context: The operator accepts a recorded event after verifying its receipt and evidence.
required_concepts.boundary: A Recovery Action cannot exceed its assessment, erase history, reuse an attempt identity, or invent effect certainty.

required_concepts.definition: The Control Center is the operator-facing application for authoring strategies, reviewing dispatch proposals, starting and observing runs, inspecting provenance, handling recovery, and reusing templates through the Orchestrator APIs.
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the human control surface for the Orchestrator.
required_concepts.domain_context: A user creates a strategy in chat, reviews its lanes, starts it, and opens the resulting run page.
required_concepts.boundary: The Control Center is not an authority source, transition engine, accepted-history writer, or substitute for underlying records.

required_concepts.definition: A Run Template is a saved user-facing preset that selects one Strategy Template version plus default parameters, adapters, limits, presentation metadata, and admission prompts for repeat dispatch.
required_concepts.formal: RunTemplate = (strategy_template_version, defaults, adapter_defaults, limits, presentation, admission_prompts)
required_concepts.plain_language: It is the button-ready configuration used to create a familiar dispatch proposal.
required_concepts.domain_context: The “two-lane dialectic” button preselects four agents, two tension pairs, synthesis, and budget defaults.
required_concepts.boundary: A Run Template is not a Strategy Template version, admitted Run Bundle, running job, or authority grant.

required_concepts.definition: A Domain Gate is a domain-owned decision boundary represented structurally as Work that emits one declared route outcome while retaining the decision’s meaning, evidence, and authority outside RWO.
required_concepts.plain_language: It lets domain decisions control flow without giving the graph ownership of the decision.
required_concepts.domain_context: A research quality owner emits accepted, revise, or reject for a synthesis artifact.
required_concepts.boundary: A route label is not the semantic verdict, authority grant, or downstream effect permission.

required_concepts.definition: An Outcome Reference is an immutable content-addressed pointer to a worker or strategy output and its media type, schema, provenance, and storage location.
required_concepts.plain_language: It lets commands and results refer to outputs without placing bulk content in structural events.
required_concepts.domain_context: A report event carries the digest and location of the Markdown report.
required_concepts.boundary: A reference is not the output content, proof of correctness, acceptance, or publication.

required_concepts.definition: A Strategy Result is the orchestrator-owned closeout view that binds terminal structural state to selected Outcome References, provenance, unresolved residue, and lifecycle status for one run.
required_concepts.formal: StrategyResult = (run_id, terminal_state, outcome_refs, provenance, residue, lifecycle_refs)
required_concepts.plain_language: It presents what the strategy produced and what remains unresolved.
required_concepts.domain_context: A dialectic result links both tension reports, synthesis, audit findings, and open questions.
required_concepts.boundary: A Strategy Result does not make its claims true, accepted, promoted, published, or externally effective.

required_concepts.definition: A Capacity Reservation is a bounded temporary claim against declared scheduler capacity for one pending or active assignment.
required_concepts.plain_language: It prevents dispatch from exceeding configured concurrent work limits.
required_concepts.domain_context: Starting an agent attempt reserves one model-worker slot until completion or lease expiry.
required_concepts.boundary: Capacity reservation is not a worker lease, provider quota guarantee, cost approval, or effect authority.
